subject: Clarify forced model plan for EU banking pilot
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ari Shah <ari@novafin.com>, Novafin Security <security@novafin.com>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify forced model plan for EU banking pilot

Team —

Novafin's security/compliance lead (copied) pushed back on any automated fallback to "open" model variants for their EU pilot. Their ask is effectively: for EU traffic, only the exact model we certify may be used — no automatic routes or fallbacks to other variants even in overload. They attached a short constraints doc (attached).

High level asks for this thread:
- Confirm whether Product + Ops are comfortable supporting a hard model-binding (forced selection) for the pilot window.
- If yes, what is the operational plan (capacity, canary, circuit-breakers) so we don't cause availability regressions?
- Security: what additional evidence (audit logs, binary artifacts, image signatures, kernel/quantization proofs) do we provide to Novafin to accept the risk profile?

I'm leaving details to you, Karthik and Marcus, but we need a short one-pager for Novafin by Wed and a clear internal plan in Jira by EOD Thu.

Attachments: novafin-request-constraints.pdf, eu-pilot-config-proposal.yaml

Thanks —
Monica
Monica Patel
Account Sales, Enterprise 
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ari Shah <ari@novafin.com>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify forced model plan for EU banking pilot

Monica —

Thanks for flagging. Quick reactions:
1) "Hard bind" (i.e., reject or queue requests when the certified variant isn't available) is a pretty heavy SLA/behavior change. We need to decide whether to:
   - Return 503 with a clear error (Novafin handles retry on their side), or
   - Queue and attempt slow-serve (increases latency and token-cost), or
   - Failover to a manually approved standby variant (requires human-in-loop approvals).

2) From Product perspective we can add a per-account route policy that enforces model-id only, but Ops will need capacity guarantees and an escape hatch for platform incidents. We should not ship without at least one emergency fallback (with manual approvals) to avoid major outages.

3) Security asks: audit logs and signed model artifact checks are straightforward. If Novafin wants cryptographic attestation of quantized weights / image signatures, we need a small infra piece (couple sprints). We can re-use the ModelSigning RFC prototype I worked on last quarter to generate signatures and an attestation token.

Next steps I propose:
- Marcus: give an ops runbook outline (capacity & emergency procedure) — can you do that by EOD Mon?
- Grace: draft a short security checklist for Novafin (what we can deliver now vs roadmap) — EOD Mon?
- Monica: I can produce a short technical note on model signing + attestation and the config flags required for a hard-bind policy.


— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Product — Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Ari Shah <ari@novafin.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify forced model plan for EU banking pilot

Folks —

Operational constraints and a practical plan below. TL;DR: we can support hard-model binding for a short pilot if Novafin accepts a defined availability SLO (lower than standard) and a clear on-call escalation path.

Operational plan (high-level):
- Capacity: reserve a dedicated pool in eu-west-1 for the certified model (minimum 3x baseline QPS for pilot). We'll surface a monthly reserved-capacity addendum to the contract.
- Canary: 24-48h canary at 5% of traffic, manual approval to ramp.
- Emergency escape: a manual override button in Console that will route to a preapproved standby image (Human approval with 2-approver flow). This is not automatic.
- Monitoring: dashboard with per-model token latency, queue length, and per-route circuit-breaker triggers.
- Incident play: if queue length > threshold for more than 2 minutes, automated throttling + paging to on-call + notify customer with templated message.

Risks / customer asks that need Product/Security signoff:
- If customer insists on absolutely zero standby / fallback, we must accept a potential for sustained 503s during platform-wide pressure. Need executive sign-off (legal aware).
- Model-attestation: we can produce signatures, but integrating attestation verification into runtime adds ~2 weeks to schedule (infra + product).

I'll drop a short ops-runbook to the Jira ticket (INF-1892) by EOD. If this plan looks acceptable, we need Monica to confirm commercial terms (reserved capacity + pilot SLO) and secure Novafin sign-off on the emergency override semantics.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Manager, Production Services
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clarify forced model plan for EU banking pilot

Thanks everyone —

This looks like the right concrete approach. Two quick operational asks from Security/Compliance side before we share the one-pager with Novafin:
1) Provide a sample audit log snippet showing model-id binding events, and proof that the runtime records the attestation token for each served session.
2) Confirm retention and exportability of those logs for customer audits (we can provide the retention policy and optional log-export config to customer-managed S3 buckets).

Monica: can you own the external one-pager (incorporate the Ops runbook and the Product note Karthik mentioned)? Karthik/Marcus/Grace/Irene will each add short sections to the draft in the shared Drive link (I've created a folder and added INF-1892 as a header).

If we can get the one-pager and the short runbook into Drive by Wed EOD, I will sign off and we can send to Novafin.

Irene
